what_this_measures: Mean frame luma (the burned-in overlay banner excluded) at three moments, to state exactly how much the camera record can and cannot discriminate.

preflight_0335Z_and_repose_0339Z.note: Room light ON. These are the frames the preflight arena inspection used: robot belly-down and flat, six legs splayed, no person or hands in frame, L2 swept arc clear, AprilTag tracker resolving 10-12 tags per view.

during_motion_034513_034754Z.note: Room light OFF. robot-1 sat at 25.0-25.1 for all 252 frames with no step anywhere in the run, so the light went out BEFORE motion started, not during it.

finding: The room light was ON at 03:35-03:39Z and OFF from before 03:45:13Z onward. Someone switched it off between the preflight inspection and the run; nothing was commanded and the robot was unaffected. This is the same person-in-the-room activity already recorded at 03:22Z, not a fault.
consequence_stated_plainly: The illumination during motion is the SAME as the 413d5402 sibling run, so the same limitation applies and is NOT claimed away: the 252 distinct frames per camera establish continuous coverage and that the chassis did not lift, shift or translate, but they do NOT resolve the ~10 mm commanded foot excursion or a thin cable. Obstacle clearance rests on the swept-volume geometry argument and the free-air currents, not on these frames. What the frames DO add over the sibling run is that the arena was separately inspected under full light at 03:35Z, six minutes before motion, and nothing entered the arena afterwards that the differencing below would have missed.

first_vs_last_frame_difference.interpretation: Near-zero over the whole 156 s on every camera, so nothing entered or left the arena and the chassis did not translate. At this exposure this is a stillness check, not an obstacle check.
